I want to recommend this awesome indie game to you all. You lead a mercenary company in a low-fantasy kind of medieval world. You have to do all the management functions of keeping your mercenary business solvent, taking contracts, hiring and firing mercenaries, choosing equipment and loadouts and managing the combat encounters on a tactical hex grid map.

The gameplay loop is just addicting. Your choices on the strategic layer directly impact the results on the tactical level, and vice versa. The combat mechanics have a lot of depth, simulating such things as a fatigue and morale. The different mercenaries are all unique individuals with different traits and backgrounds. And as the mercenaries gain experience you get to level them up and further customize them with a selection of talents and stat increases.

The AI is consistently challenging on the tactical level, and it will punish you. Also the random number generator can hose you. But oddly, this is one of the things that makes the game so re-playable. It adds that randomness that makes each campaign a unique experience, even though you're fundamentally doing the same things. I've been playing the "Lone Wolf" campaign a lot lately. In this mode you start with one well equipped badass hedge knight, but if this guy dies your campaign is over. It's fun. There's a lot of other possible starts that provide a slightly different gameplay, such as being a group of deserters, or a peasant militia.

There's a new DLC for this game about to be released in a week that adds a bunch of stuff including gladiator fights where you can enter some of your mercenaries into an arena battle where there is no option to run away. Victory or death!

I've seen this game described as a turn-based Mount and Blade, and that's not a bad take. Except there's not really mounts, and you only develop your mercenary company. There is no territory capture element in Battle Brothers. Also the troops in Battle Brothers are more like RPG characters than the troops in Mount and Blade.

I had fun playing it a while back but I think I got burned out quickly and didn't finish my playthrough. I also think I didn't rush as much as I should have to be ready for the main game crisis. But I didn't know I should.
